organization_or_family: TBMM Tutanak Dergisi, Genel Kurul minutes and research reports
licence_or_reuse_notes: Official verbatim record of the Grand National Assembly, openly published. Short quotations carried as evidence with attribution; no document is redistributed. No individual is named in anything stored, including speakers.
assessment_notes: Assessed 2026-10-29, after two of its documents had already been used without a recorded assessment. The Tutanak Dergisi is the Assembly's own verbatim record, published openly as PDFs under www5.tbmm.gov.tr and as HTML speech pages under www.tbmm.gov.tr, with no registration or paywall. Tier 1 as a DOCUMENT: what it proves is that a thing was said in the chamber on a given date. It does not make the statement itself an official finding, and most of what it carries is members speaking, so a claim drawn from it takes the assertion status of the speaker rather than of the record. ROBOTS: www.tbmm.gov.tr serves directives naming three AI agents and no wildcard group, two of which (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User) are disallowed from /*.pdf$ while GPTBot is allowed everything; www5.tbmm.gov.tr serves none (302). This project's agent matches no group, so nothing disallows its retrieval, but the intent is plain and collection stays manual: named documents fetched once each, never crawled, with the page or printed page recorded. PDFs carry a real text layer; extraction uses pdftotext in reading order, not layout order, because the transcript sets two columns, and soft hyphens are stripped before any quote is checked. PRIVACY: transcripts name the dead. Excerpts are chosen so that none does, and a name is never stored even redacted where the sentence can be avoided. Used for the Amasra 2022 casualty revision (open question 20).
Tier 1 for AGGREGATES ONLY — feeds aggregate_* tables, never incident-level evidence.

organization_or_family: İSİG Meclisi (İşçi Sağlığı ve İş Güvenliği Meclisi) work-death reports
licence_or_reuse_notes: Site-wide footer grant: free reuse on condition the source is cited. Attribution required on every derived row. Aggregate figures only; no document is redistributed and no victim name is stored.
assessment_notes: Assessed 2026-10-26. Monthly and annual work-death reports are published as HTML with a real text layer (no PDF, no OCR) from an index at isigmeclisi.org/is-cinayetleri-raporlari, paginated to 18 pages reaching back to 2013; no registration or paywall applies and no robots.txt is served (checked 2026-10-26, HTTP 404, so no directives exist to honour). The footer of every page grants reuse site-wide: “tüm yazılı ve görsel içeriği kaynak göstermek koşuluyla özgürce kullanılabilir” (all written and visual content may be used freely on condition that the source is cited), so automated collection is permitted and attribution is required. GRANULARITY: aggregate only, like SGK. A monthly report gives the month total plus breakdowns by branch of work (“Madencilik işkolunda 7 işçi”), by cause, by age band and by province, but the province breakdown spans every branch together and no per-incident rows are published, so these figures feed aggregate_* tables only and never incident rows. Two handling rules follow. The Assembly states its counts as lower bounds (“en az”) compiled from national press (64 per cent) and from colleagues, families, unions, workplace doctors and local press (36 per cent), and it counts all work deaths from all causes including traffic, heart attacks, violence and suicide, so the series is not a count of mining accidents and carries comparability notes on every row. And every monthly report ends with the names of the dead, which this project does not store or publish, so the parser cuts the roll at the memorial sentence and no stored excerpt may contain a victim name. Going direct upgrades the existing 2012-2025 annual series from a tr.wikipedia transcription to the publisher itself and extends it to monthly. Tier 2: a civil society monitoring network reporting its own compilation, above press reporting and below an official record. Partly answers open question 23.

organization_or_family: Türkiye Taşkömürü Kurumu (institutional and legal history pages)
licence_or_reuse_notes: No reuse or copyright statement is published on the pages used. Short quotations are carried as evidence with attribution; no page is redistributed.
assessment_notes: Assessed 2026-10-29. TTK is the state hard-coal enterprise and these are its own institutional and legal history pages, so for its own founding, its predecessor and its basin chronology it is a primary record, which is why tier 1 is proposed. Open HTML with a real text layer, no registration and no paywall; no robots.txt is served (checked 2026-10-29, the request returns the site's own 404 page, so there are no directives to honour). No reuse statement is published anywhere on the pages, so automated collection is recorded as not permitted and collection stays manual: named pages retrieved individually, never crawled, one source_documents row per retrieval with its sha256, and every quote machine-checked against the retrieved bytes before it is written (scripts/organization_validity.py). IMPORTANT LIMIT ON RELIABILITY: the Tarihçe page is internally inconsistent on dates. It places the TTK Ana Statüsü in its 1983 chronology while its own narrative and the legal page both date it 11 December 1984, and it cites the 1957 TKİ law as both 3460 and 6974. Being official does not make a date right, so a TTK date that conflicts with the register is recorded as a competing claim and never promoted on the strength of the tier alone (open question 40). Used for the two 1983 organization-validity corrections and the Kozlu-İhsaniye date conflict.
